newsitem.title: USA: SigmaTron sees historically soft Q1.
newsitem.headline: SigmaTron sees historically soft Q1.

text.p: SigmaTron International Inc, an independent contract maker of components and printed circuit board assemblies, said Monday it expects its fiscal first quarter results to be soft, consistent with the seasonal nature of its buisness.
"The first quarter is expected to be soft, but the backlog is growing and we expect a solid fiscal 1998," said Gary Fairhead, SigmaTron president and chief executive officer.
"...Much of our business is seasonal in nature. Generally the fourth and first quarters are slow and the second and third quarters are strong," he said in a news release. Earlier
today, the company reported record earnings for its fiscal year ended April 30, 1997 of $3.26 million or $1.11 a share on record revenues of $87.2 million.
One of SigmaTron's objectives is to add new customers whose business would help smooth out the current seasonality of our revenues, he added.
Shares of SigmaTron were trading up 1/4 to 13.
